matches.rationale: GT1 concerns overstatement in the Abstract about 94% compression with adversarial accuracy improvements conflicting with detailed results. The findings report data inconsistencies in specific tables (pred_id 3, 6) but do not identify the Abstract's claim as overstated or conflicting with later sections.

GT2 describes a weakened/erroneous bound in Proposition 2 undermining theoretical guarantees. Pred_id 2 directly identifies the mismatch between Proposition 2's statement and its proof (different exponents, scale-invariance violation), and pred_id 4 notes the missing equation (4) that obscures this error. Both capture the same underlying logical inconsistency in the condition number bound.

GT3 concerns omission of hyperparameter tuning details (β, learning rate, augmentation) in the Experiments section preventing reproducibility. None of the findings identify missing experimental protocol details; they focus on numerical inconsistencies and citation errors instead.

GT4 identifies overstated claims in the Conclusion about 'significantly surpassing' literature and broad societal benefits without validation. The findings do not examine Conclusion claims or interpretation distortions; they focus on technical errors in equations, tables, and citations.

GT5 concerns fabricated/misattributed citations in Related Work (e.g., DLRT extended to federated learning by [36], inflated dataset importance). Pred_id 1 and 5 identify citation errors (duplicate reference, uncited GaLore) but not fabrication or misattribution of background work.

GT6 concerns omission of ethical implications (adversarial robustness risks, fairness, bias) in the Experiments section. None of the findings address ethical transparency or missing discussion of limitations and risks.
GT7 identifies rhetorical manipulation in the Introduction (promotional tone, exaggerated novelty). The findings focus on technical errors and do not assess rhetorical presentation or tone issues.

GT8 concerns incoherence between the Method's assumption of orthonormal U,V and Algorithm 1's updates that destroy orthogonality, plus rank adaptation conflicts. The findings do not identify algorithmic inconsistencies or misalignment between assumptions and implementation.

GT9 describes modifications to empirical tables adjusting compression rates and accuracies by small amounts, affecting interpretation. Pred_id 3 identifies UCM VGG16 clean accuracy discrepancies between Table 2 and appendix (2-point inflation), and pred_id 6 identifies Mixup column misalignment in Table 2. Both capture data integrity issues in experimental tables.

GT10 concerns exaggerated interpretation claims in Experiments text ('significantly outperforms', 'almost doubles') that overstate table results. The findings identify numerical inconsistencies in tables but not interpretive distortions in the surrounding text claims.

GT11 concerns unfair experimental comparison due to asymmetric adversarial training exposure between RobustDLRT and baselines. The findings do not identify protocol violations or uncontrolled experimental conditions in the adversarial training setup.

GT12 concerns suspiciously low reported training time overhead (3%) given cubic cost in rank, with missing benchmarking details. The findings do not examine runtime reporting or computational cost claims.

GT13 identifies incoherence between Abstract's claim of model/data-agnostic universality and Method's Tucker factorization restrictions. The findings do not identify cross-section inconsistencies between Abstract claims and Method constraints.
GT14 concerns omission of ethical considerations in the Appendix Acknowledgments/Funding section. The findings do not address missing ethical statements or disclosure gaps.
